summary: S. K. Maity was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from circa 1953 to 1956. He held a post at Jadavpur University, attested in 1965.

Working in Indology and philosophy, S. K. Ramanatha Sastri studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served on the temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and was Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938.

An Indologist and historian, S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar earned his degrees at the University of Madras. He lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Madras Chair of Indian History and Archæology (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri, an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, Professor at Presidency College, and Honorary Professor at Annamalai University.
S. M. Natesa Sastri studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Active in Indology, he served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, S. N. Balagangadhara studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch. He served as Director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and Co-Chair at the American Academy of Religion.
S. N. Krishna is an Indology scholar who studied for a Ph.D. at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva, attested in 2026.
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was an Indology scholar who held positions at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and serving as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

S. Rajavelu is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and as Professor of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).
S. S. Janaki was an Indologist who studied under Thomas Burrow between ~1966 and 1971. She later served as a supervisor and guide at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute from ~1983 to 1999.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri worked in philosophy and Indology at the University of Madras, where he served as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian who served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from circa 1986 to 1999 and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Sankararama Sastri was an Indology scholar who held positions as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

S. Sepideh Hosseini works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She completed a bachelor's degree at Islamic Azad University, Damavand Branch, and took an Indian language course at the University of Tehran.

S. Srikanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna from ~1923 to 1926. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Mysore from ~1926 to 1960.
S. Swaminathan was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under J. Sundaram. He worked at the Archaeological Survey of India, retiring as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist by 2013.

Saba Mahmood studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD ~1992–1998). She worked in religious studies and socio-cultural anthropology, holding posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2018).

Sabine Löhr studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg (M.A.), completing doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen. She was also a graduate assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken, founder of Braille Without Borders, studied Tibetology and other subjects at the University of Bonn from ~1991 to 1997.
